comment: D-SINK-19. state.json's `activeKey`: which source is active, by key, in the
plugin's own 0600 file instead of as a provider URL in the host's shell.json.
Run by BOTH tests/Model.test.js and tests/test_state.py, because the rule is
implemented twice -- Model.activeKeyText / parseState in QML JS, and
normalize_active_key / normalize_state in the helper -- and a rule in two
languages gets one fixture (engineering rule 12, dev branch). The helper is the
half that matters most here: it REBUILDS the document from default_state() and
copies the keys it knows, so a key it has not been taught is ERASED by the next
`state favorite add`, and for THIS key that means the plugin reads as not
configured at all. savedSearches and hiddenGroups both carry that warning; this
one would have been visible.
Sections, and who runs each. A name here that is not a key of this file is the
join rule 13 warns about, and Model.test.js checks the list against the keys:
`parse`   BOTH. The raw JSON value of `activeKey` and the string both readers
must produce. A key naming no record is KEPT at parse time on
purpose: whether it resolves is a property of the LIST, not of the
value (Model.activeKeyOf is where the resolution happens).
`remove`  BOTH. Removing a source: the pointer the state is left with
(Model.removeSource and the helper's remove_source_record, R3).
`resolve` JavaScript only. Model.activeKeyOf over a stored key and a list.
`adopt`   JavaScript only. Model.adoptActiveSource's ORDER (lead ruling R1):
a fresh URL first, then the state's key, then the entry's mirror,
then nothing. The helper never resolves the active source and never
migrates one: the migration reads the host's bar entry and the
helper knows nothing about shell.json by design (D15).
`order`   JavaScript only. Model.pointerWritePlan (R5): state before entry,
and the entry waits for a parked state save.
recordsNote: The records `adopt` and `remove` build states from, by key. A case's `keys` list names which of them the state carries; `new` below is a URL none of them has, whose key is d5977d8a.

parse.name: absent reads as no active source
a three-digit suffix is the widest the grammar admits
surrounding whitespace is trimmed, not refused
an empty string is no active source
uppercase hex is not a key (the writers emit lowercase)
seven hex characters is not a key
nine hex characters is not a key
a four-digit suffix is not a key
a path traversal is not a key, which is what keeps it out of a directory name
a slash is not a key
a key with an interior space is not a key
a URL is not a key, and this is the shape a hand-edited old file would carry
a number is not a key
a boolean is not a key
a list is not a key
an object is not a key

resolveNote: Model.activeKeyOf: the stored key, but only while it names a record the same state carries. The dangling cases are the ones a CLI `state source remove`, an eviction and a hand-edited file all produce.

resolve.name: dangling: the record it named is gone
not a key, with a record that would otherwise match nothing

adoptNote: Each case: a state (`keys`, `activeKey`), the bar entry as settingsFrom read it, the plan flags (`adoptUrl` / `adoptEpg`, default true: a value the service has not consumed), and what adoptActiveSource must answer. `sources` is the count the state comes out with; `epgOnActive` is the active record's epgUrl afterwards.

adopt.name: R1 step 1: a fresh URL beside a resolving key -- the URL is adopted, added, and the key MOVES (the review's P1: the first version returned the key and discarded the URL)
R1 step 1: a fresh KNOWN URL beside a different active key -- that record becomes active, nothing is added
R1 step 1: the same URL again (re-set by the user) -- active already, nothing moves, the entry is still rewritten to take the URL out
R1 step 1 refused: an invalid URL beside a resolving key -- the key is kept exactly as it was and the refusal is reported (D16)
R1 step 1 refused, with no active source at all: the refusal is the only thing there is
R1 step 1, the old shape: a URL on the entry and no key anywhere -- the migration
R1 step 1 over a dangling state key: the URL is adopted and the dangling value replaced
R1 step 2: no URL, a resolving state key -- the key, and nothing to write
R1 step 2: the state's key beats a DIFFERENT mirror on the entry, and the mirror is rewritten
R1 step 3: no URL, no state key, the entry's sourceKey names a record -- the mirror recovers it
R1 step 3: a mirror naming a record that is gone is not a pointer
R1 step 3: a non-key on the entry is not a pointer
R1 step 4: nothing anywhere -- a dangling state key is CLEARED, not left for the next reader
R1 step 4: an empty install stays empty and writes nothing
R1 consumed: a URL the service already adopted (the host's stale echo, rule 9) is NOT read -- the key wins, and the entry is rewritten because the URL is still on it
R1 consumed, over NO state key: the stale echo does not resurrect a source the user removed through the CLI
R4: a fresh EPG input alone reaches the ACTIVE record (D-SRC-02), and the entry is rewritten to take it out
R4: a consumed EPG input is not adopted twice
R4: an EPG input the record already holds changes nothing
R4: an invalid EPG input is not adopted, and still asks for the entry write that takes it out
R4: an EPG input with no active source to land on is not adopted (it stays the guide's fallback until a source exists)
R1+R4: a fresh URL and a fresh EPG in one write land on the record the URL named
D-SRC-10 kept: a fresh URL beside a CONSUMED EPG -- the EPG was the previous source's and does not follow

removeNote: Each case: the records the state carries, its activeKey, the key removed, and the pointer and count the state is left with. `ok` false is an unknown key: no change on either side (the helper reports unknown_source).

remove.name: R3: removing the ACTIVE record clears the pointer
R3: removing an INACTIVE record leaves the pointer alone
R3: removing the only record, which is active
R3: removing with no active source changes nothing about the pointer
R3: an unknown key removes nothing and moves nothing

orderNote: Model.pointerWritePlan: the two writes a pointer change makes, in order. `keyMoved` is whether the state's key changes in this call; `dirsReady` and `savePending` are the service's start-up gate (saveState parks a write until stateInitProc has made the 0600 file). The entry NEVER goes out ahead of a parked state save.

order.name: R5: the key moved and the dirs are ready -- state, then entry, now
R5: the key moved before the dirs are ready -- the state save parks and the entry WAITS for it (the interrupted-migration case)
R5: the key moved, dirs ready, an earlier save still parked -- the save flushes first
R5: the key did not move but an earlier save is parked behind the dirs -- the entry waits
R5: the key did not move, an earlier save is parked, dirs ready -- flush it, then the entry (nothing else would wake a wait)
R5: nothing to save -- the entry, now
R5: nothing to save and dirs not ready -- the file already says what memory says, the entry may go
R5: no input at all is the cautious no-move, dirs-not-ready answer
